preamble: The voiced aspirated velar stop [ɡʱ] loses its oral closure and only the breathy component survives as [h]. In Italic, PIE *gʰ (merged with *ǵʰ) gave Latin h through a fricative stage reconstructed as Proto-Italic *χ (hostis, hiems). In Middle Indo-Aryan, intervocalic Sanskrit gh was reduced to h (megha > meha, laghu > lahu), a change continued in the modern languages. Other branches keep a stop (Greek kʰ, Germanic and Slavic g).

examples.note: 'stranger, enemy'; via Proto-Italic *hostis (*χ); cognate with Proto-Germanic *gastiz (English guest)
'winter'; Latin merges palatovelar *ǵʰ with plain *gʰ as h
Middle Indo-Aryan reduction of intervocalic aspirates to h; also Assamese meh, Gujarati meh, Punjabi mī̃h (Turner CDIAL 10302)
gh > h intervocalically; the Hindi form shows later metathesis lahu- > halu-
